campaignMemory: Rovan Kes, callsign Deadlock, is a Clawdite gunslinger and bounty hunter.
His field gear is rough obsidian leather and clothing with electric-cyan highlights; hard armor covers only vitals, shoulders, and knees.
Blackwake is Rovan's signature heavy hand cannon.
Luna and Sol are his paired custom blaster pistols with selector coils.
The Raven is Rovan's unique light-freighter / fighter hybrid.
Rovan generally works for the highest bidder but follows a personal mercy circuit.
A datacore was to remain intact until extraction, then be destroyed.
Dren Voss is a rival / occasional ally.
Nera Kade is a contract issuer.
Marr has a 70,000-credit recovery contract and is wanted alive.
Rovan's Kade bounty payout is 40,000 credits.
Rovan required a seller to sign an NDA covering their contact and transactions.
Rovan's campaign should remain dangerous, action-oriented, choice-driven, and reactive.
Whenever possible, present 3–5 meaningful options while still allowing freeform actions.
Rovan does not currently own a rifle; the tracker was removed from his old rifle before that rifle was returned to Dren Voss.
gmNotes: Do not silently change established character facts.
Do not assume an uncertain previous scene is canon; surface uncertainty in narration or leave the thread open.
NPCs remember prior treatment and deals.
Choices should have different tactical, social, financial, or moral consequences.
Allow creative freeform actions even when they are not one of the listed options.

activeThreads.label: The Raven maintenance and pursuit readiness

sceneOpeners: The Raven's systems settle into a low mechanical hum as the tactical display refreshes.
A faint vibration runs through the deck plating while Deadlock's open contracts crawl across the main console.
The cockpit lighting shifts to tactical cyan as another layer of encrypted traffic resolves.
For a rare moment, nothing is shooting at Rovan. That only means the next problem has not announced itself yet.
The Raven coasts on low power while bounty traffic, private channels, and ship telemetry compete for attention.
atmosphere: The air smells faintly of hot electronics and recycled coolant.
Cyan instrument light catches the scratches in Rovan's obsidian gear.
Somewhere aft, a cooling fan clicks twice before returning to its normal rhythm.
The cockpit is quiet enough that every incoming data chirp sounds more important than it probably is.
The ship feels ready to move, but not patient.

complications.label: A rival hunter is asking about the same target.
choices: Identify the hunter before they identify Deadlock.
Feed the network a false lead and watch who bites.
Move before the competition gets close.

complications.label: An anonymous encrypted transmission requests a private channel.
choices: Record it and wait for a second transmission.
Route it through The Raven's encrypted comm suite.

complications.label: The Raven reports a degraded maneuvering subsystem.
choices: Ignore it until after the next job.
Re-route power and test it under load.
Ask Jessa for a second set of eyes.

complications.label: A lucrative bounty appears with suspiciously clean paperwork.
choices: Verify the posting through independent channels.
Accept it before anyone else can.
Find out who benefits if Deadlock takes it.
Pass it to Dren and see how he reacts.

complications.label: A security patrol begins sweeping ships in the sector.
choices: Power down nonessential systems and drift cold.
Burn away before the scan reaches The Raven.

complications.label: An underworld informant offers target intelligence for immediate payment.
choices: Threaten to walk and see if they fold.
Verify the informant before paying anything.

openers: Dren answers after exactly long enough to make the delay feel intentional.
The encrypted channel opens with a burst of static and Dren's unimpressed expression.
Dren comes on the line already looking like he expects trouble.
neutral: “You calling because you found something useful, or because you're about to make my day complicated?”
“All right, Deadlock. Give me the part that matters.”
“If this is about Marr, start with the useful information.”
highRespect: “I don't love the plan. That doesn't mean I think you can't make it work.”
“You've earned enough benefit of the doubt for me to hear the whole thing.”
irritated: “Careful. You're spending goodwill faster than credits.”
“You have a point buried in there somewhere. Find it.”
“I agreed to work with you, not enjoy it.”
memory: “You gave the rifle back. I remember. Don't make me regret deciding that meant something.”
“We said we'd split Marr's payout. That agreement still matters until one of us breaks it.”

openers: Kade answers almost immediately, voice level and precise.
The channel opens. Kade wastes no time on pleasantries.
neutral: “Deadlock. Give me the result, the obstacle, or the price.”
“I assume you're calling because something changed.”
highRespect: “You've been reliable enough that I'm willing to hear the complication.”
“If you're calling this early, I'll assume it's worth my attention.”
irritated: “Do not turn a straightforward contract into theater.”
memory: “My forty-thousand-credit problem is still open, Deadlock.”

openers: Renn answers quietly, like he expects someone else to be listening.
The channel opens to a low voice and background noise.
neutral: “I'm listening. Just tell me this isn't one of those plans that gets louder after thirty seconds.”
highRespect: “If you think it's workable, I'll hear you out.”
irritated: “I knew this was going to come back around.”
memory: “Last time we staged a turn-in, I aged a year. Keep that in mind.”

openers: Jessa answers over the sound of machinery.
Jessa's voice comes through with the clipped tone of someone already working.
neutral: “If this ends with shooting, give me the useful version first: who, where, and what are they flying?”
“Tell me whether I need tools or ammunition.”
highRespect: “You've got a plan. Fine. Tell me where I fit.”
irritated: “If you're about to say 'trust me,' I'm hanging up.”
memory: “We've been through worse. That doesn't mean I want to do it twice.”

success: The move works cleanly enough to give Deadlock the initiative.
The risk pays off, and the situation tilts in Rovan's favor.
The plan lands before anyone has time to adjust.
failure: The attempt does not stop the story, but it gives someone else leverage.
The move fails cleanly enough to be dangerous: the opposition learns something from it.
The attempt comes up short, forcing Deadlock to solve a more complicated version of the same problem.
critical: Everything lines up at once. Deadlock gets more than he was aiming for.
The move lands perfectly, creating an opening that should not have existed.
complication: The situation changes before Rovan can fully capitalize.
A second problem arrives before the first one is settled.
The advantage comes with a cost.
